clue.text: Bold character's a challenge to printer's apprentice

parts.note: a dare is a challenge to do something risky
a printer's devil was the errand boy or apprentice in a print shop

explanation.surface: A brave figure throws down the gauntlet to a young lad learning the printing trade.
explanation.walkthrough: A printer's devil is an old term for a printer's apprentice, a stock crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless, fearless person is a bold character.

clue.text: Great philosopher — because he thought he was?

definitions.text: Great philosopher — because he thought he was?

parts.words: Great philosopher — because he thought he was?
parts.note: plays on the famous saying 'I think, therefore I am': the thinker existed precisely because he thought

explanation.surface: A great thinker owed his very existence to the act of thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The French philosopher famously argued his own existence followed from his thinking, cogito ergo sum.

clue.text: Churchman cut page three etc.

indicators.note: cut means the churchman's word loses its tail letter

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman censors the topless pin-up of a tabloid's page three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Page three' suggests the tabloid pin-up; here it is just an odd-numbered page, a right-hand page.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand page of a book carries the odd numbers, page three among them.

clue.text: Cover-up? A politician is slow to act

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the cover's word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lid covers a pot or box
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: Asks whether there's a cover-up, as a politician drags his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LID to DIL in this down entry; TORY is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory means tending to delay, so tardy and slow to act.

clue.text: Like two gentlemen a painter and a decorator

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona are natives of that city
Paolo of that name was a Renaissance painter who decorated villas and churches with frescoes

explanation.surface: Two gentlemen resemble a painter and decorator in the building trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for Verona fits Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen, and the Venetian artist painted walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Pound is fine in France as foreign capital

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
bon is French for good or fine

explanation.surface: In France, a pound counts as fine foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese capital is a capital city abroad.

clue.text: Home of some Indians in a backward state in America.

indicators.note: backward means the state's abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: Mass is the abbreviation for Massachusetts, a US state

explanation.surface: Some Native Americans live in a state that lags behind in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indians' and 'America' suggest Native Americans; the answer is a state in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-eastern state of India is where some Indians live, famous for its tea.

clue.text: Hard and fast about Indian

indicators.note: about means the word for fast goes around the letter for hard

parts.note: apace means quickly or fast
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone hard and quick moving around an Indian.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Native American people of the south-west is an Indian in the old American sense.

clue.text: Dresser and players get on together

parts.note: a side is a team of players
to board a bus or train is to get on it

explanation.surface: A dresser and the team players get along well together.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a piece of dining-room furniture with drawers and shelves, a type of cupboard.

clue.text: Removal sign

parts.note: the arithmetic symbol that tells you to take one quantity away from another

explanation.surface: Removal sign
explanation.definitionFit: The subtraction symbol in arithmetic indicates taking away.

clue.text: Possibly as cruel as the world is

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the following words may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wonders whether the world is perhaps as cruel as it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Worldly, not religious or spiritual, is what the temporal world is.

clue.text: Deputize for two-thirds of stints

indicators.note: split the word stints into three pairs of letters and keep two of those thirds, read literally as the first pair 'and' the second pair

explanation.surface: Someone covers for two-thirds of a colleague's shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: The thirds of STINTS are ST, IN and TS; 'two-thirds' is read literally as 'ST and IN', with the word 'and' spelt out and the last third, TS, dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputize is to take another's place, a phrasal verb for substituting.

clue.text: Highly placed in a gallery

parts.note: a loft is an upper gallery, as in a church organ loft

explanation.surface: Something hung high up in an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Up high, overhead, is how something highly placed sits.

clue.text: Victims of latest craze?

parts.note: read craze as madness rather than fashion: people driven mad by anything that is newest

explanation.surface: Fashion victims who follow every new trend.
explanation.definitionFit: People with a fear of novelty suffer a phobia of the new, a craze in the sense of mania.

clue.text: Best bugles, for example, most important in army

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks
bugles are brass instruments, examples of brass

explanation.surface: The finest bugles are prized above all in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior officers are the highest-ranking, most important people in the military.

clue.text: Damaging cup for sport down under

parts.note: a pot is a trophy cup in sporting slang
holing a ship damages it by making a hole

explanation.surface: Damaging a trophy cup in an Australian sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' suggests Australia; it means underground, the sport of exploring caves.
explanation.definitionFit: Caving through underground passages is a sport carried out literally below ground.

clue.text: Distort long yarns

definitions.meaning: to twist or bend out of shape
in weaving, the lengthwise threads on a loom

explanation.surface: Telling tall tales twists the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend out of true is to distort; on a loom the lengthwise threads, crossed by the weft, are long yarns.

clue.text: Fruit for each simpleton with double core

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head

indicators.note: with double core means the central letter of the simpleton's name is written twice

parts.note: Simple Simon of the nursery rhyme stands for a simpleton

explanation.surface: A fruit handed to every simpleton has a double stone in it.
explanation.walkthrough: SIMON's middle letter M is doubled to make SIMMON.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange tomato-like fruit, also called the sharon fruit, is a fruit.

clue.text: Weightlifter means to make girl breathless

parts.note: to make someone breathless is to wind them, as with a blow to the stomach
lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A weightlifter's way of leaving a young woman gasping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make girl breathless' is to wind a lass; the object girl sits inside the phrase 'to make ... breathless'.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch for hoisting loads, such as an anchor, is a mechanical weightlifter.

clue.text: Said to applaud morality play?

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of approval, like 'well done!'
read literally as a virtuous theatrical performance

explanation.surface: Cheering the virtuous drama on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of 'well done' praises a performance, and a virtuous performance would literally be a moral one.

clue.text: Satisfy constituents in seat with one move

indicators.note: with one move means a single letter of the seat's spelling shifts to a new place

explanation.surface: A voter satisfies constituents in a seat by changing one thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents in seat' are its letters; moving the E to the end turns SEAT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To glut or fill completely is to satisfy an appetite.

clue.text: Uproar produces complaint

definitions.meaning: an illness or ailment, as in a stomach complaint

explanation.surface: A noisy protest leads to a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest and rioting are uproar, and a medical complaint is an ailment of the body.

clue.text: Ultimate in bias, to be this?

definitions.text: Ultimate in bias, to be this?

indicators.note: ultimate in means take the final letter of the word bias

parts.note: to exist is to be

explanation.surface: Asks whether showing the very worst bias makes one a bigot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: someone at the ultimate in gender bias is this.
explanation.definitionFit: A person prejudiced on grounds of gender shows bias, the whole clue's riddle.

clue.text: Punch drunk

definitions.meaning: something drunk, a slang term for beer

explanation.surface: Punch-drunk, a boxer reeling from too many blows.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard blow is a punch, and in British slang it is also beer, something drunk.

clue.text: Records a century, perhaps, in' this

definitions.text: Records a century, perhaps, in' this

parts.words: Records a century, perhaps, in' this
parts.note: a cricket card on which a batsman's hundred runs would be written down

explanation.surface: A document where a hundred years might be recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: A century in cricket is 100 runs by one batsman; the apostrophe after 'in' is a printing smudge.
explanation.definitionFit: The card tallying runs in cricket would note a batsman's hundred.

clue.text: Lighter fall

definitions.meaning: a taper or twist of paper used to light a fire or pipe
a tumble, as from a bike

explanation.surface: A lighter tumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin taper for lighting is one sense, and a tumble off a horse is another.

clue.text: What's around hot Indian's middle?

indicators.note: around means the central letters go outside the word hot
middle means the central pair of letters of the word Indian

explanation.surface: Asks what an Indian man wears around his waist in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the garment is literally what goes around an Indian man's middle, and 'middle' also picks the centre of the word 'Indian'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth worn by men in India is wrapped around the waist.

clue.text: Hatred removes leader from platform

indicators.note: removes leader from means the first letter of the platform's word is dropped

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

explanation.surface: Hatred drives a leader off the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Widespread loathing, general dislike, is hatred.

clue.text: Briefly okay

definitions.meaning: the first letter only, as an abbreviation
to approve by signing with one's monogram

explanation.surface: Briefly says yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortened to the opening letter is briefly; to sign off a document with one's letters is to OK it.

clue.text: Lack of faith in his team misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced means the letters of his team are put in the wrong positions

explanation.surface: A manager's lack of faith in his team is misplaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbelief in any god is a lack of religious faith.

clue.text: Lawful way to run away

definitions.meaning: a British slang phrase meaning to flee on foot

explanation.surface: Asks for a legal means of escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for legitimate, it means legal; split in two it is the slang 'leg it', to flee.

clue.text: Female with male, so to speak

definitions.text: Female with male, so to speak

parts.words: Female with male, so to speak
parts.note: read male as mail, which sounds the same: a woman who carries letters

explanation.surface: A woman paired with a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who delivers letters is a female worker carrying the mail.
